assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall state from spin-orbit coupling in graphene, the Z2 classification, and the HgTe/CdTe realisation opened the whole field of topological insulators. It is a clear case of experiment confirming a bold theoretical idea about a new state of matter, and band-structure theory explains the measured edge conduction quantitatively.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical framework and Z2 invariant; Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive experimental observation in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The credited trio gives a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction and the 3D insulator work (Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele, Hasan, Zhang) are not in these credited names.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation across many materials and ARPES, transport and theory; the interpretation is stable and the field is mature, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested because of the BHZ proposal and the 3D topological insulator discoveries, which this entry does not credit.
Whether the committee prefers a broader topological-insulator citation than the 2D quantum spin Hall effect alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance, and especially coherent spin-dependent tunnelling through crystalline MgO, combines a first-principles prediction with experimental realisation. It underlies read heads and MRAM, so it is a rare case of quantitative electronic-structure theory leading to a technology used widely.
assessment.attribution: Butler and collaborators predicted the symmetry-filtered tunnelling in Fe/MgO/Fe from DFT; Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated the large effect in 2004. Miyazaki's 1995 room-temperature TMR is an equally strong claim, and Moodera (not credited) also reported it, so the limit of three names leaves a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Twenty years of use in devices and many independent replications. The physics is well understood and recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the 2007 GMR prize overlaps.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 prize for GMR may weigh against it.
Credit between Miyazaki, Parkin, Yuasa, Butler and uncredited contributors such as Moodera and Mathon is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT gives a controllable, non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions, and explains the Mott transition and the Kondo-like quasiparticle peak. Combined with DFT it has become a standard tool for real correlated materials, which is close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt founded the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar built the mapping to an impurity problem and later DFT+DMFT. The credited trio is reasonable, but Metzner is not in the list and Kotliar's and Georges's contributions are partly with Krauth and Rozenberg.
assessment.maturity: Decades of application, with stable and well-benchmarked methodology. Quantitative accuracy for real materials still has limits, so confirmation is mainly through successful comparison with spectra rather than a single decisive experiment.
uncertainties: A method and theory prize may be less clearly a physical discovery than the committee prefers.
Metzner, Rozenberg and Krauth are not in the credited names, leaving the allocation incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of skyrmion lattices in chiral magnets and then in thin films and at interfaces established a new topological spin texture with emergent electrodynamics and potential for low-power storage. It is a genuine discovery in magnetism, where theory explains the stabilisation via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's group (with Mühlbauer et al.) found the A-phase skyrmion lattice, Tokura imaged real-space skyrmions and drove the materials work, Wiesendanger showed atomic-scale interface skyrmions. The theoretical prediction by Bogdanov and colleagues is not credited, and in the supplied credit this is a hard attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated, but the application story (racetrack memory) has not been realised, so the discovery stands on scientific grounds and may be seen as still developing.
uncertainties: Theory credit to Bogdanov and others is outside the credited names.
Choosing among experimental groups for first observation is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity, created moiré quantum materials as a new platform for tunable correlation physics. It is a striking case of theory predicting a number that experiment then found.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald and Bistritzer provided the continuum-model theory and Jarillo-Herrero's group the 2018 experiments; the two-laureate configuration captures the core of the story, though Bistritzer's contribution is real and the experimental team and the Cao-Fatemi-et-al work are collective.
assessment.maturity: Only about eight years old, with many independent confirmations but unsettled interpretation of the superconductivity and correlated phases, so it may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Bistritzer and other experimental contributors are left out under a two-name proposal.
Timing may be premature compared with more mature candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters, as shown by the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and later quantum-gas microscopes. These provide quantum simulation of lattice models relevant to condensed matter and a link to correlated electron theory.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and colleagues proposed the Hubbard realisation and Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott transition; Cirac is credited for later simulation proposals. Greiner-Bloch-Zoller captures the founding steps, but Hänsch and Jaksch, and the Kasevich group also deserve consideration.
assessment.maturity: A mature field with extensive independent confirmation, but the 2001 and 2018 prizes for BEC and for laser cooling are nearby, and the quantitative payoff for materials remains partly a promise.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes and with other quantum-simulation entries.
Credit among Zoller, Cirac, Bloch and Greiner, and Jaksch (not credited), is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Angle-resolved photoemission mapped the Fermi surface, d-wave gap and pseudogap of the cuprates, giving direct momentum-resolved access to the electronic structure of correlated materials. The measurement connects directly to the spectra that theory must explain.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano, Shen and Takahashi each led pioneering high-resolution ARPES work; the three-name configuration is plausible, though the instrument and technique go back to Hüfner, Plummer, Eberhardt and others, and this is a technique prize more than a single discovery.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, but the central problem (the mechanism of cuprate superconductivity) remains unresolved, so the discovery is a measurement approach rather than a final understanding.
uncertainties: A prize for technique and measurement rather than a unique discovery.
Instrumental developers are not among the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single colour-centre spins, notably the NV centre in diamond, enable room-temperature quantum sensing and spin-photon interfaces. It has real technological reach and solid physical understanding, with spectroscopy tied to experiment.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single NV spin detection and coherent control; Awschalom extended the platform to SiC and other defects, while Lukin's theory contributions are among the four credited. The three-name selection is workable but reflects a judgement that I cannot verify independently.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed it, but applications continue to evolve, and I regard it as a little less decisive as a single discovery than the condensed-matter candidates above.
uncertainties: Choice among Awschalom, Jelezko, Wrachtrup and Lukin is not clear-cut.
Distinction between a platform of many defect types and a single discovery.
